answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the falcon check immediately, the ember audit keeps the resolved set and the tide replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 54 aliases thus pays the reading cost 54 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
